- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward → adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots → reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 5–7 days to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.2) and price is trending up, model underestimates upside → increase forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.  
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile → add 0.5–1.5% buffer to short-term forecasts.  
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive (e.g., +0.3+ in 3 days), model lags in adjusting → delay forecast upward by 1–2 days and scale up by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
